title: As Snow Flows and Goes Sounding...
text:
As snow flows and goes sounding

from having been silence, so my forgetting,

from the summits of being where it has slept,

descends to natal time and flows now.


Now the soot in the forge is celestial,

and the creaking of the wheel with tow

of the ropemaker, and the plane curls

an immortal honey of still.


The yoke team returns from winning the valley

with its dragging lance, and the bell

returns to pass between the light and the bridge.


The market returns to dress the street

with arcades. Everything returns and pours forth

the forever-yesterday eternally.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Ridruejo's return of village memory, with snow becoming sound and yesterday flowing eternally.

title: Deserted Love
text:
Whoever gives a heart to this minute,

stiff and frozen, to this flowing without harmony,

to this painful and cold blood of mine,

to this dry grief without voice or mourning;


whoever polishes edges on the rough diamond,

whoever returns to the bird its lost guide,

whoever makes solitude and company,

voice and silence for the absolute song;


whoever gives me back all my landscapes

and sees, gathered in my stillness,

the longed-for coast and veil of my journeys;


whoever turns health back to me with her wound,

whoever dresses my dreams in her garments,

formless longing! will fulfill my life.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem as an invocation to the one who can restore landscape, guide, wound, and life.

title: The Idyll That Was Only a Gaze
text:
It is, if I enter painful forgettings,

your never-heard voice that cries out.

You were eternal afterward, and an eternal appointment

that the minute of encounter did not keep.


Like an orbit troubled by its center

that returns in flight and avoids contact,

with the certainty of love written,

you lived far away and beat within.


Neither caress nor voice knew each other,

nor did the air suspect our loves,

which slept in a time without hours.


Love had eyes, sowing without flowers,

and in those tearless eyes that saw me,

the tears you weep will still see me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the unrealized idyll as a love made only of gaze, distance, and belated tears.

title: To a Statue of a Nude Woman
text:
To a statue of a nude woman


Naked and vertical, but girded,

the line of the earth to the indolence

        of a flesh that yields, when the perfection

of dream begins its measure.


Matter without love, but kindled

by the faithful number of purity,

        where cold flesh is dressed

without the taste of time and life.


O docile to the eyes and set apart

from the fire of blood, mute glory

        in ecstasy of lifted earth!


Ancient youth, fresh and worn,

that afflicts the passion of its memory

        in this eternity so calm.
editorial_note: The source catalog title points to the millstone poem, but the displayed body is the nude-statue sonnet.

title: Assault
text:
Soft and firm, your hand.

Your heart did not tremble; it was an instant

of calm and surface

in your voice like silver with sand

and in the damp slate of your eyes.


It has been now, absent,

when touch remembers a caress,

and inward through the blood your aroma raises

the swell and burns your golden skin.


I suffer, estranged, in this new hand

with its almond-tree emotion,

which beats and creates as it remembers. I pass it

over the familiar objects: iron,

wood, glass, wool-yours-

and an electric discharge of roses

makes them living flesh.
editorial_note: The translation keeps touch as delayed assault, turning ordinary objects into rose-charged living flesh.
